solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A clerk's odd half-cut hairstyle

indicators.note: half-cut is slang for drunk, and drunk letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: the letters of the three words, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: An eccentric office clerk turns up tipsy with a half-finished haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-cut' looks like a haircut description beside 'hairstyle', but it is British slang for drunk and signals the shuffle of A CLERK'S ODD.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreadlocks are a recognised hairstyle of long matted or twisted ropes of hair.

clue.text: Small dog I had raised to excavate

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising something turns it upside down, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: a pug is a small snub-nosed dog breed
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: A little dog, once lifted, gets set to dig.
explanation.walkthrough: PUG and I'D are joined first, then the whole run is read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To dig up is the phrasal verb for removing earth to uncover something, an everyday synonym of excavate.

clue.text: Duke, perhaps, stealing wife from another one?

indicators.note: stealing something away from a holder leaves that holder without it

parts.note: another duke: the Duke of Wellington, victor of Waterloo
W is the standard abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: One aristocrat runs off with another nobleman's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another one' means another duke, Wellington; take away the W for wife and the jazz bandleader Duke Ellington remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Duke Ellington was a jazz bandleader whose nickname was Duke, so he is an example of a Duke, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Sheer quality of Sunshine Soap ad being broadcast

indicators.note: broadcasting scatters seed far and wide, so the letters land in a new order

parts.note: the fourteen letters of the advert's words

explanation.surface: A television commercial for a brand of soap called Sunshine goes on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' suggests television to match the soap advert, but here it means scattered.
explanation.definitionFit: Diaphanous fabric is so fine and light that it is see-through, which is what sheer means of cloth.

clue.text: Holds good bastion in the wars

indicators.note: something in the wars has been knocked about and damaged, so its letters are battered out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sound fortress holds firm through the fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holds good' reads as a fort holding out, but it is the definition, in the formal sense of a rule still applying. 'In the wars' is a British idiom for being battered or injured.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtain has an intransitive formal sense of being established or prevailing, as when a custom still applies today.

clue.text: Reported hoard found on lake in mountainous region

indicators.note: in a down clue, one thing placed on another sits above it, so the first piece comes first
something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the words count by their spoken form

parts.note: a cache is a hidden store, pronounced like cash
a mere is a lake, chiefly in English place names

explanation.surface: News of buried treasure discovered beside a lake high in the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken together, 'cache mere' gives the region's name. A mere is an English word for a lake, as in Windermere.
explanation.definitionFit: Kashmir is a Himalayan region divided between India, Pakistan and China, known for its mountain ranges.

clue.text: House record label is after soprano initially

indicators.note: to come after something means following it, so that piece goes second
initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: first letter of the word
EMI is a well-known British record label

explanation.surface: A house-music label chases after a soprano to sign her first.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a semi is short for a semi-detached house, one sharing a wall with its neighbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Semi is the everyday British shortening of semi-detached house, a dwelling joined to one neighbour.

clue.text: Watching and complying with missing outside broadcast

indicators.note: a thing missing from a word is no longer there, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: to obey is to comply with
OB is the standard abbreviation for an outside broadcast

explanation.surface: A viewer watches and follows instructions while missing the live outside broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: An outside broadcast is a TV programme made on location, abbreviated OB; removing it from OBEYING leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye something is to look at it closely, so eying is a synonym of watching.

clue.text: Dig tunnel badly, revealing some tolerance

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase standing for the adjective

indicators.note: work done badly is botched and disordered, so the letters come out jumbled

parts.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: A shoddy tunnelling job shows that someone is being too easygoing with the diggers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revealing' reads as part of the tunnelling scene, but the whole phrase 'revealing some tolerance' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An indulgent person is lenient and permissive, readily allowing others their wishes.

clue.text: Pottery company relocates — worry for breakage

indicators.note: something broken falls into pieces that can be put back in another order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A china maker moves premises, fearing its stock will get smashed in transit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relocates' looks like the anagram signal but it is part of the fodder; the signal is 'for breakage'.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal Worcester is a famous English porcelain manufacturer founded in Worcester in the eighteenth century.

clue.text: Irritate insect lover

parts.note: to gall is to vex or irritate
an ant is a common insect

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lover' looks like an object of 'irritate', but it is the definition at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallant is an old word for a man paying court to a woman, a suitor or ladies' man.

clue.text: Fabled hill that is found in South Dakota

indicators.note: whatever is found in a place sits inside it, so these letters are enclosed

parts.note: SD is the postal abbreviation for South Dakota
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A legendary hill stands somewhere in South Dakota, perhaps among the Black Hills.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a rocky outcrop on a hilltop, common on English moors.
explanation.definitionFit: Storied means celebrated in stories or legend, so it is a direct synonym of fabled.

clue.text: Censure those people around India with second religious belief

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one set of letters wraps about the others

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly
them refers to those people
I is India in the NATO alphabet
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: Critics condemn a group in India for their newer form of faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like 'another' religious belief, but it is the usual abbreviation for a unit of time, sitting beside India inside the pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: Pantheism is the doctrine that God is identical with the universe and nature, a theological creed.

clue.text: Star turn caught by everyone

indicators.note: something caught by another is held within its grasp, so it sits inside

parts.note: all means everyone
a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: A star performer's act is greeted by the whole audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star turn' is a stock phrase for a headline act, but 'Star' alone is the definition and 'turn' is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Algol is a well-known variable star in the constellation Perseus, sometimes called the Demon Star.

clue.text: Staff take more time to deal with deliveries

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a stick or rod, such as a conductor's or a relay runner's

definitions.text: take more time to deal with deliveries
definitions.note: a two-word verb phrase, BAT ON
definitions.meaning: second meaning: in cricket, to continue batting against the bowled balls

explanation.surface: Workers need extra time to handle all the parcels arriving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' reads as employees and 'deliveries' as parcels, but in cricket a delivery is a ball bowled, and to bat on is to keep batting.
explanation.definitionFit: A baton is a short rod or stick, and a staff is likewise a carried rod or pole.

clue.text: Author book company lifted — about chapters one and two finally

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for book

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting something turns it upward, so its letters read bottom to top

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company
ca, for circa, means about
CC is the plural abbreviation for chapters
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so only the closing letter is kept

parts.note: last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A writer's publishing house is bought out, and the deal concerns his first two chapters.
explanation.walkthrough: Only CO is reversed; the rest are standard abbreviations strung in order, with 'two finally' giving just O.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Boccaccio was a fourteenth-century Italian writer, best known for The Decameron.

clue.text: Tropical fruit tree has thorn protecting bunch?

indicators.note: to protect something is to shield it on all sides, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a spine is a sharp thorn on a plant
a crew is a gang or bunch of people; the question mark flags the loose synonym

explanation.surface: A spiky tropical tree guards its cluster of fruit with thorns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bunch' suggests a cluster of fruit but means a group of people.
explanation.definitionFit: The screw pine, or pandanus, is a tropical tree with spirally arranged leaves and large edible fruits.

clue.text: Stress appeal is to be found in children's book heroine

parts.note: it is old slang for sex appeal

indicators.note: a thing found in a place is located inside it, so these letters go within

parts.note: Alice of Lewis Carroll's Wonderland books
taken as written

explanation.surface: A storybook heroine's charm becomes the focus of attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' looks like a link verb but supplies its own letters, set inside ALICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Writers italicise a word to emphasise it, so setting it in slanted type is a way to stress it.

clue.text: Those against hollowed out universal support — who was asked?

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for the noun, the one who was asked

parts.note: the cons are the arguments or people against

indicators.note: a hollowed-out thing has had its inside removed, so only the shell of the word stays

parts.note: first and last letters of the word
a tee supports a golf ball

explanation.surface: Opponents have gutted any general backing, and someone asks who was even polled.
explanation.walkthrough: A tee is the little peg on which a golfer rests the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A consultee is a person whose advice or opinion is sought, the one who has been consulted.

clue.text: Drink cuppa with most of cinnamon roll eaten

indicators.note: food that is eaten goes inside the eater, so one piece is swallowed by the other

parts.note: a cuppa is British slang for a cup of tea

indicators.note: most of something is nearly all of it, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a quill is a rolled stick of cinnamon bark

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys a cup of tea with a cinnamon bun, most of it already gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cinnamon roll' suggests a pastry, but a rolled stick of cinnamon bark is called a quill. A cuppa is British slang for a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Tequila is a Mexican spirit distilled from agave, a type of alcoholic drink.

clue.text: One moved out day before receiving a signal

indicators.note: to receive is to take in, so one piece holds the other within it

parts.note: an eve is the day before an event
taken as written
a cue is a signal to act

explanation.surface: Someone left home the day before, having been sent a signal to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Day before' is a single idea: the eve of an event, as in Christmas Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: An evacuee is a person removed from a place of danger to safety, as children were in wartime Britain.

clue.text: Become very warm when in decay

indicators.note: one thing in another is inside it, so these letters are enclosed

parts.note: rot is decay
as can mean when, as in 'as I arrived'

explanation.surface: Things heat up as they start to rot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When' gives AS, as in 'as the sun rose'.
explanation.definitionFit: To roast informally means to feel uncomfortably hot, as when people say they are roasting in summer.

clue.text: Trembling like mother of cygnets

parts.note: as means like, in comparisons
a pen is a female swan, and cygnets are young swans

explanation.surface: Someone is shaking like an anxious swan guarding her young.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is used as an adjective here, after the aspen tree whose leaves quiver in any breeze.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspen is a literary adjective meaning quivering, from the tree whose leaves flutter constantly in wind.

clue.text: The French put in more meat with rice dish

indicators.note: anything put in somewhere ends up inside it, so these letters go within

parts.note: più is Italian for more, a musical direction
la is French for the, feminine

explanation.surface: A French cook adds extra meat to a rice dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More meat' reads as a phrase, but 'more' belongs to the wordplay and 'meat with rice dish' is the definition. PIÙ is the musical term for more, as in più mosso.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilau is a spiced rice dish, often cooked with meat in stock, from South Asian and Middle Eastern cooking.

clue.text: Note to perform vocally, ignoring small tremolo

parts.note: a quaver is a musical note, an eighth note

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out of account, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: to sing is to perform with the voice
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A singer is told to sing a note without too much wobble in the voice.
explanation.walkthrough: A quaver is the British name for an eighth note.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremolo is a trembling effect in music, and quavering is a trembling of the voice.

clue.text: Chokes eating English plums

indicators.note: whatever is eating something takes it inside, so one piece swallows the other

parts.note: to gag is to choke or retch
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Someone splutters while eating English plums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eating' looks like the diner's action, but tells you one piece goes inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: Gages are varieties of plum, such as the greengage, so the word names a kind of the fruit.

clue.text: Big figures of company deficit — with little current

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company
a loss is a deficit
I is the physics symbol for electric current; little signals the abbreviation

explanation.surface: A firm's headline figures show a large loss and little cash flowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big figures' reads as large sums in the accounts, but means giant statues.
explanation.definitionFit: Colossi are gigantic statues, like the Colossus of Rhodes, so they are huge human figures.

clue.text: Poling a boat topless round back of Trinity? It needed this first

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it, so one piece encloses the other
topless means without a top, so the first letter is removed

parts.note: punting is propelling a flat boat with a pole

indicators.note: the back of something is its end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone punting on the river at Trinity College, Cambridge, finds the boat needed releasing from its mooring first.
explanation.walkthrough: Trinity is a Cambridge college where students punt on the Cam. The definition refers back to the boat: before it can be poled away, it must be cast off.
explanation.definitionFit: A moored punt must be released from its tethering rope before it can move, so freeing its knot came first.

clue.text: Responsibility assigned to under-secretary

parts.note: a task that is on someone is assigned to them
US is the abbreviation for under-secretary

explanation.surface: A duty is handed down to a junior government official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assigned to' looks like a link phrase but supplies letters, as in 'the drinks are on me'.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a burden or duty that rests on someone, so it is a synonym of responsibility.

clue.text: Become a minister and submit to PM's whims?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to be ordained into the church, taking holy orders
second meaning: to obey the instructions given by a boss

explanation.surface: A newly appointed government minister must do whatever the Prime Minister fancies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' and 'PM' paint a political picture, but the first meaning is a church minister, who is ordained by taking holy orders.
explanation.definitionFit: Clergy are said to take holy orders on ordination, and anyone who obeys commands is following instructions given.
